newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Regional prices seen steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Regional prices seen steady to firm.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices may consolidate this week, but the market will probably not post hefty gains in the absence of fresh offtake, regional traders said on Monday.
The spot expiry in Japan and heavy rains in Thailand which hindered tapping last week lifted sentiment, but any rise in prices will be seen as an opportunity to sell, the traders said.
"I think the market can consolidate and hold at these levels, but it won't race away," a senior dealer in a Western commodity trading company told Reuters.
"The rain could further support the prices. But I don't expect any sharp rise if the market lacks new fresh factors," a Thai trader said.
The meteorological department in Bangkok warned of more heavy rain drenching the south, Thailand's major rubber-growing region.

"The weather in Thailand has been supportive of prices. But any upside in the market is fairly limited since supplies remain ample and major buying remains a bit weak," one Singapore-based rubber trader said.

The Thai benchmark RSS3 for November shipment was quoted last week at around US$1.22-$1.24 a kg FOB Bangkok against $1.19-$1.23 last week. The same grade was quoted around $1.24-$1.25 a kg FOB Bangkok for January shipment.
Latex prices were barely changed from last week and stood at 95 U.S. cents a kg FOB Bangkok.
Auction market sources said only about 230,000 kg of rubber sheets entered the market last week compared with 371,392 kg the previous week.
Malaysian prices would also rebound this week if demand picks up even if only in the form of short-covering, dealers said.

"I don't think the weather is really going to make a difference any more," said a Malaysian dealer, referring to rains this month which have reduced tapping and supply of raw materials into the market, but failed to lift prices in any way.
In the event of a fresh round of buying, the benchmark RSS1 and SMR20 rubber could rise at least "three and five cents", said another dealer.
"This is a conventional estimate as usually the market goes through the roof after a long period of bearishness," he said.

November buyers for RSS1 were quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at Malaysian 308.50 cents a kg at the close of the market on Friday. November SMR20 buyers were seen at 306.50 cents.
The two grades have been trading in a tight range since September, after an active round of short-covering by European, Chinese and Middle East buyers.
Dealers said demand for latex was still the softest among all grades and tracking sales was difficult because deals were done discreetly by producers selling at low levels.

"You can't keep latex in its original form for too long and producers are selling cheap, but they don't want to suppress the market further with the information," said a trader with a foreign dealing house.
Trading houses quoted drum latex on Friday at 232 cents a kg.
Indonesian benchmark SIR20 rubber prices were also likely to remain in a narrow range this week on the back of expected slow demand and adequate supply, dealers said.
"The market has been so weak for at least a month. It is likely to remain so in the coming week due to continued weak demand," one dealer in the north Sumatran city of Medan said.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for November/December deliveries were likely to stay between 55.25-55.75 U.S. cents/lb FOB Medan and to 54.75-55.25 cents FOB Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 54.50-55.00 cents FOB Jambi and Pontianak.
Dealers in Indonesia's main commodity city of Medan said selling SIR20 below the 60.00 cents/lb level is already considered to be unprofitable, let alone below 55.00 cents.
Dealers in the western Sumatran city of Padang and the southern Sumatran city of Palembang said they managed to sell SIR20 at 54.50-54.75 cents/lb, barely enough for them to survive upon.
One Jakarta dealer said pale crepe remained weak. It was last sold at 152 cents/kg FOB Semarang for prompt shipment to Japan, but did not specify the type of crepe sold.
Dealers said RSS1 rubber rose one cent/kg, but prices remain generally weak.
RSS1 was sold last week at 123 cents/kg for November/December deliveries against the previous 122.0-122.50 cents, dealers said.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
